newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees "drastic drop" in coffee production.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees "drastic drop" in coffee production.

text.p: The commercial manager of Colombia's powerful National Coffee Growers' Federation said a "drastic drop" in the country's output during the current coffee year justified market fears about tight supply. "The drastic drop in the crop more than justifies the fears of buyers," said John Naranjo, who spoke in a closing address to a meeting of Latin American coffee officials in this city in central-western Colombia.
Revising previous estimates of Colombia's production in the 1996/97 coffee year, he said output could drop as low as 10.4 million 60-kg bags, from 12.9 million bags in 1995/96.
Federation officials have said unusually heavy rains during last month's flowering period, and an increase in production costs, were among factors weighing on output during the current coffee year.

Naranjo spoke shortly after Oswaldo Aranha, head of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Federation, told Reuters on the sidelines of the meeting here that Brazil would have to draw on its official coffee stocks totaling 13.2 million 60-kg bags to meet demand at home and overseas.
As with Brazil, Colombia also intends to draw on federation stocks, Naranjo said.
He did not elaborate on how much of the 6 million 60-kg bags of green coffee in federation inventories would be brought to market but said that "the majority of it is in excellent condition."
Naranjo declined to give a crop estimate for the 1997 calendar year, saying it was too soon to come up with a reliable figure.
He said production between October 1996 and September 1997 would not surpass 11 million 60-kg bags, however, and warned that it may very well be no more than 10.4 million bags.
